message.content:
Take B_n(x) = x^n on [0,1]. Pointwise limit: f(x) = 0 for x < 1, f(1) = 1. Convergence fails uniformly: sup|x^n − f(x)| = 1 for all n, since x^n approaches 1 as x approaches 1 from below.

If f is continuous, Baire's category theorem ensures uniform convergence. Discontinuous limits prevent uniformity.
